items.q: Mai ______ three novels by that author since January.
items.vi: Từ tháng Một đến giờ Mai đã đọc ba cuốn tiểu thuyết của tác giả đó.
items.explanation: Since January links a past starting point to now, so the present perfect has read is needed; the past simple and past perfect cut the action off from the present.

items.q: My sister ______ the ending of the film in my ear so that nobody else in the cinema could hear.
items.vi: Chị tôi thì thầm vào tai tôi đoạn kết của bộ phim để không ai khác trong rạp nghe thấy.
items.explanation: So that nobody else could hear tells you the words were said very quietly: whisper. Shout is loud, and announce / declare mean to say something openly to everyone.

items.q: We ______ a lot of money on new furniture for the living room.
items.vi: Chúng tôi đã tiêu rất nhiều tiền vào đồ nội thất mới cho phòng khách.
items.explanation: The collocation is spend money on something. You pay for something, a thing costs money, and take does not go with money in this way.

items.q: Relax – it is only a tiny scratch on the car door. Don't ______.
options: put all your eggs in one basket
bite off more than you can chew
kill two birds with one stone
make a mountain out of a molehill
items.answer: make a mountain out of a molehill
items.vi: Bình tĩnh đi, chỉ là một vết xước nhỏ xíu trên cửa xe thôi. Đừng có chuyện bé xé ra to.
items.explanation: Make a mountain out of a molehill = treat a small problem as a big one. The others mean risking everything on one plan, taking on too much, and achieving two things at once.

items.q: We waited an hour outside the cinema, but Nam never ______.
items.vi: Chúng tôi đợi cả tiếng ngoài rạp chiếu phim, nhưng Nam chẳng bao giờ xuất hiện.
items.explanation: Turn up = arrive or appear. Turn down = refuse or lower the volume, turn off = switch off, and put up needs an object (put up a poster).

items.q: Nam ______ at the concert last night – I saw him at home at nine o'clock.
items.vi: Tối qua Nam không thể nào ở buổi hòa nhạc được – lúc chín giờ tôi thấy cậu ấy ở nhà mà.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle expresses a confident conclusion that something was impossible in the past. Mustn't have is not used for deduction; needn't have and shouldn't have talk about necessity and advice.

items.q: The coach with ______ we trained for the swimming competition has moved to another club.
items.vi: Huấn luyện viên mà chúng tôi đã tập luyện cùng cho giải bơi đã chuyển sang câu lạc bộ khác.
items.explanation: After a preposition (with) the relative pronoun for a person must be the object form whom: with whom we trained. Who cannot follow a preposition, whose needs a noun after it, and which refers to things.

items.q: Linh has visited ______ countries in Asia, but she has never been to Japan.
items.vi: Linh đã đi thăm vài nước ở châu Á, nhưng cô ấy chưa từng đến Nhật Bản.
items.explanation: Countries is a plural countable noun, so it takes several (= a few, more than two). Much and a little go with uncountable nouns, and every must be followed by a singular noun.

items.q: Could you ______ the last scene to me? I didn't understand why the hero left.
items.vi: Bạn giải thích cảnh cuối cho mình được không? Mình không hiểu tại sao nhân vật chính lại bỏ đi.
items.explanation: Explain something to someone = make it clear. Complain = say you are unhappy, persuade takes a person as object, and you argue with someone, not a scene.

items.q: Remember ______ the front door when you go out this evening.
items.vi: Nhớ khóa cửa trước khi con ra ngoài tối nay nhé.
items.explanation: Remember to do = don't forget a task that is still to come. Remember doing looks back at a memory of something already done, so it does not fit an instruction.

items.q: Nam still went to school ______ he had a bad cold and a sore throat.
items.vi: Nam vẫn đi học mặc dù cậu ấy bị cảm nặng và đau họng.
items.explanation: A contrast followed by a full clause (he had a bad cold) needs the conjunction although. Despite and in spite of are followed by a noun or -ing form, and however is an adverb that cannot join two clauses like this.

items.q: Could you ______ me to call Grandma tonight? I always forget.
items.vi: Bạn nhắc mình gọi cho bà tối nay nhé? Mình lúc nào cũng quên.
items.explanation: Remind someone to do something = help them not forget. Suggest and recommend do not take someone to do, and mention means to speak briefly about something.

items.q: I wish I ______ the film last night – everyone at school is talking about it.
items.vi: Giá mà tối qua tôi đã xem bộ phim đó – ở trường ai cũng đang bàn về nó.
items.explanation: A wish about the past (last night) takes the past perfect: wish + had seen. Saw would be a wish about the present, and would see is for the future.

items.q: Could you ______ me a favour and return this book to the library?
items.vi: Bạn giúp mình một việc, trả cuốn sách này về thư viện được không?
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is do someone a favour. Make, give and take do not combine with favour in this meaning.

items.q: The film ______ in Da Lat last year, which is why the scenery looks so familiar.
items.vi: Bộ phim được quay ở Đà Lạt năm ngoái, vì thế cảnh trong phim trông rất quen thuộc.
items.explanation: The film does not shoot itself, so the passive is needed, and last year puts it in the past simple: was shot. Is shot is present, and shot / has shot are active.

items.q: This time next week, my family ______ in our new house on the other side of town.
items.vi: Vào giờ này tuần sau, gia đình tôi sẽ đang sống trong ngôi nhà mới ở phía bên kia thành phố.
items.explanation: This time next week points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous will be living is used. Will live states a plain future fact, and are living is present.

items.q: Mum asked me where ______ the TV remote after the film.
items.vi: Mẹ hỏi tôi đã để cái điều khiển ti vi ở đâu sau khi xem phim.
items.explanation: In a reported question the word order is subject + verb (no inversion, no did), and asked moves the past simple back to the past perfect: where I had put. The other three keep the inverted order of a direct question.

items.q: After a long talk, my parents and I are finally ______ about my plan to study music.
items.vi: Sau một cuộc nói chuyện dài, cuối cùng bố mẹ và tôi cũng đã đồng quan điểm về kế hoạch học nhạc của tôi.
items.explanation: On the same page = agreeing, sharing the same understanding. In the same boat = in the same difficult situation, under the weather = slightly ill, over the moon = very happy.

items.q: My sister is really keen ______ Korean pop music and knows every song by heart.
items.vi: Chị tôi rất mê nhạc pop Hàn Quốc và thuộc lòng mọi bài hát.
items.explanation: The adjective keen takes the preposition on: keen on something. Interested in, fond of and good at are the patterns learners mix it up with.

items.q: Please don't ______ while Grandma is telling her story – wait until she finishes.
items.vi: Đừng ngắt lời khi bà đang kể chuyện – hãy đợi bà kể xong đã.
items.explanation: Interrupt = start speaking while someone else is still talking. Repeat, describe and pronounce all need an object and do not fit wait until she finishes.

items.q: My parents couldn't ______ how to use the new TV remote, so I showed them.
items.vi: Bố mẹ tôi không tìm ra cách dùng cái điều khiển ti vi mới, nên tôi chỉ cho họ.
items.explanation: Work out = find the answer to something by thinking. Carry out = perform a task, set out = begin a journey, and work up = build up (an appetite, courage).

items.q: The more pocket money you save now, ______ you can spend on the school trip.
items.vi: Bây giờ bạn càng để dành nhiều tiền tiêu vặt, thì bạn càng có nhiều tiền để chi cho chuyến đi của trường.
items.explanation: The double comparative pattern is the more ..., the more ...: both halves need the plus a comparative, never a superlative.

items.q: By the time the film ended, the painkiller ______, and my tooth hurt again.
items.vi: Đến lúc bộ phim kết thúc thì thuốc giảm đau đã hết tác dụng, và răng tôi lại đau.
items.explanation: By the time + past simple marks a point in the past before which the other action was already complete, so it takes the past perfect: had worn off (stopped having an effect). Has worn off and wears off are present tenses.

items.q: The bookshop ______ a twenty per cent discount on all novels this week.
items.vi: Tuần này hiệu sách giảm giá hai mươi phần trăm cho tất cả tiểu thuyết.
items.explanation: A shop offers (or gives) a discount. Make, do and bring do not collocate with discount.

items.q: The shop assistant ______ that the phone was cheaper online, so we didn't buy it there.
items.vi: Nhân viên cửa hàng thừa nhận rằng chiếc điện thoại mua trên mạng rẻ hơn, nên chúng tôi không mua ở đó.
items.explanation: Admit that = agree that something (often unwelcome) is true. Deny is the opposite, refuse is not followed by a that-clause, and promise that would not lead to we didn't buy it.
